chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Jallab, from al-Hudhayni, from Ibn Arafat, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wants to pollinate the palm tree, when it was such that it would not bear (fruit) nor irrigate, so let him take two small dried fish, and let him grind these between the two grinding plates. Then he should sow a little of it in every sprout from it, and he should keep the remainder in a clean bundle, then make it to be in the heart (centre) of the palm tree. He would benefit, Allah (Exalted is He) Willing'.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Islamic ruling on using fish for pollinating date palms?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on agricultural etiquette, this hadith illustrates the practical application of natural remedies (adwiya tabi'iyya) within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that efficacy relies on divine permission (bi-idhn Allah). It reflects the Prophetic tradition of utilizing local, organic resources for sustenance, linking agricultural success to both scientific observation and spiritual reliance. The method of using dried small fish as a nutrient-rich pollination aid highlights the holistic view of nature in Shia scholarship, where material means are coupled with spiritual intent.
